title: Top coherent cohomology of a separated finite-type scheme is finite-dimensional
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $d\geq0$ be an integer, and let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is $d$. For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], the coherent cohomology group $H^d(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space (one with a finite basis). No properness, smoothness or algebraic-closedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Prove the assertion by strong induction on $d$, simultaneously for all separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all coherent modules. Such a scheme is Noetherian: its finite affine cover has finite-type $k$-algebras, which are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$); local Noetherianity is exactly [pqf-def-locnoeth], and finite type includes quasi-compactness. For $d=0$, [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] applied to the identity closed immersion gives $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite-dimensional over $k$. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], $M=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ is a finite $A$-module. If $a_i$ span $A$ over $k$ and $m_j$ generate $M$ over $A$, the finitely many $a_i m_j$ span $M$ over $k$. Since $H^0=\Gamma$, this proves the base case; zero modules and the empty scheme have zero cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, induction and dimension-zero paragraph

proof.text: Fix $d>0$ and assume the assertion in every smaller dimension. Finiteness in a fixed degree is preserved by extensions: use the $k$-linear long exact sequence of [pqf-def-cohomology] and [lem-pc-e2-cohomology-finite-extension] with $R=k$. The finite filtration in [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] therefore reduces $H^d(X,\mathcal F)$ to $H^d(X,i_*\mathcal I)$, where $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is integral closed and $\mathcal I$ is a nonzero coherent ideal. By [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] this is $H^d(Z,\mathcal I)$. The closed subscheme is separated finite type over $k$, and its dimension is at most $d$ (every chain in a closed subspace is a chain in $X$). If $\dim Z<d$, [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] makes this group zero. It remains to treat an integral separated finite-type scheme of dimension $d$ and a nonzero coherent ideal on it.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, extension closure and integral closed-subscheme reduction

proof.text: We will repeatedly use the following consequence of the induction hypothesis: on any Noetherian separated finite-type scheme, a coherent module supported in a closed subset of dimension at most $d-1$ has finite $H^{d-1}$. Indeed filter it by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes]; the supports of subquotients remain inside its support by exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. For each quotient $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$, its support is exactly $i_j(Z_j)$: [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] identifies its stalks on and off the closed subset, and a nonzero coherent ideal on an integral scheme has nonzero generic stalk and closed support by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], hence has full support. Each integral support has dimension $e\le d-1$. Closed-pushforward cohomology [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] reduces its degree-$d-1$ group to the integral support: if $e=d-1$ apply the induction hypothesis; if $e<d-1$ use [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]. Extension closure [lem-pc-e2-cohomology-finite-extension] then gives the claimed finiteness. This also handles supports which are not pure dimensional and the zero module.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, induction for the lower-dimensional ideal quotient and later cokernel

proof.text: Now write $X$ for the integral dimension-$d$ scheme. For a nonzero coherent ideal $\mathcal I$, its generic stalk is the entire function field. The quotient $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] and has closed support by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]; it misses the generic point. This proper closed subset is nowhere dense since $X$ is irreducible, so [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] bounds its dimension by $d-1$. Step 3 makes $H^{d-1}(X,\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)$ finite. The long exact sequence of [pqf-def-cohomology] gives $H^{d-1}(X,\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)\to H^d(X,\mathcal I)\to H^d(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Thus it suffices to prove finiteness for the structure sheaf: the kernel is a quotient of the first finite vector space and the image a subspace of the last.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, ideal exact sequence reducing to the structure sheaf

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and use its integral-source/relative-ampleness refinement [lem-weil-pbc-integral-chow-relatively-ample]. Obtain $\pi:Y\to X$ proper, $Y$ integral, $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ an immersion, a nonempty open $U$ where $\pi$ is an isomorphism, and $\mathcal L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$ relatively ample for $\pi$. By [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension], both $Y$ and $X$ have the dimension of the common nonempty open $U$, namely $d$. Apply [lem-pc-relative-kill-by-twisting] with base $X$, proper morphism $\pi$, and coherent $\mathcal O_Y$. Choose $n\ge0$ sufficiently large that $R^p\pi_*\mathcal L^{\otimes n}=0$ for all $p>0$. This theorem assumes properness of $\pi$, not of $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, Chow modification, relative ampleness and higher-image vanishing

proof.text: Set $\mathcal G=\pi_*\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$; it is coherent by [lem-pc-coherent-hi], since $\pi$ is proper and $X$ locally Noetherian. Choose a projective coordinate $x_a$ nonzero at the generic point of $j(Y)$; at least one exists since the standard coordinate opens cover projective space. Its $n$th power restricts to a global section $s$ of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ nonzero at the generic point (for $n=0$ take $1$). Here the transition rule for $\mathcal O(n)$ in [def-pc-projective-space-twist] identifies coordinate powers with these sections. The corresponding map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G$ is injective: a local function whose product with $s$ is zero pulls back to zero in the function field of the integral $Y$, hence is zero in the function field, and therefore in the local domain, of $X$, because $\pi$ is an isomorphism on a dense open. On a smaller nonempty open inside $U$ where $s$ does not vanish it is an isomorphism. Its coherent cokernel $\mathcal Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] has closed support [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] missing the generic point, of dimension at most $d-1$ by [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop]. Notice that a nonzero section need not be nowhere vanishing on all of $U$; the smaller open is essential.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, nonzero section and coherent small-support cokernel

proof.text: From $0\to\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q\to0$, the long exact sequence [pqf-def-cohomology] gives $H^{d-1}(X,\mathcal Q)\to H^d(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^d(X,\mathcal G)$. Step 3 makes the left term finite. It is enough that the right term be finite, by the same kernel/image argument as step 4. Since all positive higher direct images of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ vanish, [lem-pc-m1-leray-acyclic-pushforward-linear-comparison] applied to $\pi$ and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives a $k$-linear isomorphism $H^d(X,\mathcal G)\cong H^d(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, cokernel reduction and Leray comparison

proof.text: By [lem-chow-closed-model], the immersion $j$ identifies $Y$ with a dense open in its scheme-theoretic projective closure $\overline Y\subseteq\mathbf P^N_k$. This closure is integral: it is irreducible because it is the closure of an irreducible space; on an affine open meeting $Y$, the ideal of the scheme-theoretic closure is the kernel of restriction to the integral open, so the quotient embeds in its function field and is a domain. Thus [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] gives $\dim\overline Y=\dim Y=d$. The coherent invertible module $\mathcal O_{\overline Y}(n)$ restricts to $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$; the identification follows directly from the coordinate transition functions $(x_i/x_j)^n$ of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-top-degree-open-restriction-surjective] to this Noetherian closure and its quasi-compact open $Y$ to get a $k$-linear surjection $H^d(\overline Y,\mathcal O_{\overline Y}(n))\twoheadrightarrow H^d(Y,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$. The source is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-projective-coherent-finiteness], since $\overline Y$ is projective over the Noetherian ring $k$. Its quotient is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, projective closure and surjective top-degree restriction

proof.text: Step 8 proves finiteness of $H^d(X,\mathcal G)$; step 7 proves it for $\mathcal O_X$; step 4 proves it for every nonzero coherent ideal on every integral dimension-$d$ scheme. The smaller integral supports in step 2 contribute zero. Starting with $H^d(X,0)=0$, induction along the finite filtration in step 2 proves the assertion for every coherent $\mathcal F$. This closes the strong induction on $d$.

source.place: Tag 0A3M, label lemma-top-cohomology-coherent, conclusion of the induction
